newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir relief craft held up, waits for repair cable.
newsitem.headline: Mir relief craft held up, waits for repair cable.

text.p: An unmanned Russian cargo craft due to head for the Mir space station on Friday is almost certain to be held up while vital cabling needed to repair Mir's damaged power system is loaded, officials said on Thursday.

"The postponement process was started last night. It's most likely it will not go tomorrow," a spokesman for Russia's Military Space Forces said. A spokesman for Moscow's Energiya corporation, which makes the cable, said it could take two or three days to get the spare length to the Baikonur launch pad.
Military Space Forces chief spokesman Sergei Gorbunov told Reuters experts would be considering whether to replace some of the long-planned cargo with other supplies needed to repair Mir.

The station, with two Russians and a British-born American astronaut on board, lost some power from its solar panels and all the air from a holed module after a collision during a manual docking on Wednesday with a Progress cargo craft similar to the one due for launch.
Gorbunov said the loss of power would make the docking of the new Progress mission "very difficult".

Energiya Rocket Corporation spokesman Sergei Gromov said only a very short length of the cable, perhaps no more than a metre, was needed for the repair. "It should take no more than two or three days to get it to Baikonur," he said. The cable is designed to withstand very great extremes of temperature.
